results.summary_before: This project implements an FIR filter with adaptable coefficients that can be configured via a serial interface. The filter uses a symmetric step response to reduce memory requirements, and coefficients can be updated by enabling a configuration mode. It has been tested with impulse and step responses, and requires an external microcontroller or simple buttons for configuration and data input. The design is useful for learning about digital filters.
results.summary: This project implements an FIR filter with adaptable coefficients that can be configured through the input pins. The filter uses the symmetric step response property to store only half the coefficients, reducing memory requirements, and coefficients can be updated by enabling a configuration bit. It was tested with impulse and step responses, and can be driven by any microcontroller or even buttons and LEDs. The design is useful for learning about digital filters.

results.summary_before: Implements a simple PLC-style programmable logic controller in Verilog that reads eight digital inputs and drives eight digital outputs based on programmed control rules. It mimics the scan cycle of a PLC: read inputs, execute logic, update outputs. The design can be used with switches and LEDs for testing, and optional external hardware includes buttons and relays. It requires no external hardware and can be tested with a logic analyzer or LEDs.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design implements a true random number generator that harvests entropy from the jitter of free-running ring oscillators. It outputs an 8-bit random byte after whitening the sampled bitstream to remove bias. The module uses a handshake protocol with ready/valid signals to indicate when data is available. Testing involves streaming bytes to a host PC and running statistical tests like NIST SP 800-22, requiring a Tiny Tapeout demo board and an RP2040 microcontroller for data capture.

It outputs an 8-bit random byte after whitening the sampled bitstream to remove bias. The module uses a handshake protocol with ready/valid signals to indicate when data is available. Testing involves streaming bytes to a host PC and running statistical tests like NIST SP 800-22, requiring a Tiny Tapeout demo board and an RP2040 microcontroller for data capture.
